checker_type.description: The checker type to use for the check. If the monitored resource type is 'servicedirectory_service', 'checker_type' must be set to 'VPC_CHECKERS'. Possible values: ["STATIC_IP_CHECKERS", "VPC_CHECKERS"]
checker_type.rationale: Infrastructure routing choice with no direct security impact.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

display_name.description: A human-friendly name for the uptime check configuration. The display name should be unique within a Stackdriver Workspace in order to make it easier to identify; however, uniqueness is not enforced.
display_name.rationale: Display metadata with no security impact.

log_check_failures.description: Specifies whether to log the results of failed probes to Cloud Logging.
log_check_failures.rationale: Logging failures is good practice but not enforced as a security policy since it is not directly exploitable.

period.description: How often, in seconds, the uptime check is performed. Currently, the only supported values are 60s (1 minute), 300s (5 minutes), 600s (10 minutes), and 900s (15 minutes). Optional, defaults to 300s.
period.rationale: Frequency setting with no direct security impact.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Organisational field, not a security control.

selected_regions.description: The list of regions from which the check will be run. Some regions contain one location, and others contain more than one. If this field is specified, enough regions to include a minimum of 3 locations must be provided, or an error message is returned. Not specifying this field will result in uptime checks running from all regions.
selected_regions.rationale: Geographic setting with no direct security impact.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for the request to complete (must be between 1 and 60 seconds). [See the accepted formats]( https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/reference/google.protobuf#google.protobuf.Duration)
timeout.rationale: Operational setting with no direct security impact.

user_labels.description: User-supplied key/value data to be used for organizing and identifying the 'UptimeCheckConfig' objects. The field can contain up to 64 entries. Each key and value is limited to 63 Unicode characters or 128 bytes, whichever is smaller. Labels and values can contain only lowercase letters, numerals, underscores, and dashes. Keys must begin with a letter.
user_labels.rationale: Organisational metadata with no security impact.

content_matchers.description: The expected content on the page the check is run against. Currently, only the first entry in the list is supported, and other entries will be ignored. The server will look for an exact match of the string in the page response's content. This field is optional and should only be specified if a content match is required.

content_matchers.content.description: String or regex content to match (max 1024 bytes)
content_matchers.content.rationale: Functional content setting with no direct security impact.

content_matchers.matcher.description: The type of content matcher that will be applied to the server output, compared to the content string when the check is run. Default value: "CONTAINS_STRING" Possible values: ["CONTAINS_STRING", "NOT_CONTAINS_STRING", "MATCHES_REGEX", "NOT_MATCHES_REGEX", "MATCHES_JSON_PATH", "NOT_MATCHES_JSON_PATH"]
content_matchers.matcher.rationale: Functional configuration setting with no direct security impact.

content_matchers.json_path_matcher.description: Information needed to perform a JSONPath content match. Used for 'ContentMatcherOption::MATCHES_JSON_PATH' and 'ContentMatcherOption::NOT_MATCHES_JSON_PATH'.

content_matchers.json_path_matcher.json_.description: Options to perform JSONPath content matching. Default value: "EXACT_MATCH" Possible values: ["EXACT_MATCH", "REGEX_MATCH"]
content_matchers.json_path_matcher.json_.rationale: Functional configuration setting with no direct security impact.

content_matchers.json_path_matcher.json_.description: JSONPath within the response output pointing to the expected 'ContentMatcher::content' to match against.
content_matchers.json_path_matcher.json_.rationale: Functional configuration setting with no direct security impact.

http_check.description: Contains information needed to make an HTTP or HTTPS check.

http_check.body.description: The request body associated with the HTTP POST request. If 'content_type' is 'URL_ENCODED', the body passed in must be URL-encoded. Users can provide a 'Content-Length' header via the 'headers' field or the API will do so. If the 'request_method' is 'GET' and 'body' is not empty, the API will return an error. The maximum byte size is 1 megabyte. Note - As with all bytes fields JSON representations are base64 encoded. e.g. 'foo=bar' in URL-encoded form is 'foo%3Dbar' and in base64 encoding is 'Zm9vJTI1M0RiYXI='.
http_check.body.rationale: Functional setting with no direct security impact.

http_check.content_type.description: The content type to use for the check. Possible values: ["TYPE_UNSPECIFIED", "URL_ENCODED", "USER_PROVIDED"]
http_check.content_type.rationale: Functional setting with no security impact.

http_check.custom_content_type.description: A user provided content type header to use for the check. The invalid configurations outlined in the 'content_type' field apply to custom_content_type', as well as the following 1. 'content_type' is 'URL_ENCODED' and 'custom_content_type' is set. 2. 'content_type' is 'USER_PROVIDED' and 'custom_content_type' is not set.
http_check.custom_content_type.rationale: Functional content setting with no direct security impact.

http_check.headers.description: The list of headers to send as part of the uptime check request. If two headers have the same key and different values, they should be entered as a single header, with the value being a comma-separated list of all the desired values as described in [RFC 2616 (page 31)](https://www.w3.org/Protocols/rfc2616/rfc2616.txt). Entering two separate headers with the same key in a Create call will cause the first to be overwritten by the second. The maximum number of headers allowed is 100.
http_check.headers.rationale: Functional setting; security is addressed via mask_headers policy.

http_check.mask_headers.description: Boolean specifying whether to encrypt the header information. Encryption should be specified for any headers related to authentication that you do not wish to be seen when retrieving the configuration. The server will be responsible for encrypting the headers. On Get/List calls, if 'mask_headers' is set to 'true' then the headers will be obscured with '******'.
http_check.mask_headers.rationale: When Authorization or other authentication headers are present, leaving mask_headers false exposes those credentials in plain text via the GCP API on Get/List calls.

http_check.path.description: The path to the page to run the check against. Will be combined with the host (specified within the MonitoredResource) and port to construct the full URL. If the provided path does not begin with '/', a '/' will be prepended automatically. Optional (defaults to '/').
http_check.path.rationale: Functional setting with no security impact.

http_check.port.description: The port to the page to run the check against. Will be combined with 'host' (specified within the ['monitored_resource'](#nested_monitored_resource)) and path to construct the full URL. Optional (defaults to 80 without SSL, or 443 with SSL).
http_check.port.rationale: Operational setting with no direct security impact.

http_check.request_method.description: The HTTP request method to use for the check. If set to 'METHOD_UNSPECIFIED' then 'request_method' defaults to 'GET'. Default value: "GET" Possible values: ["METHOD_UNSPECIFIED", "GET", "POST"]
http_check.request_method.rationale: Request method choice with no direct security impact.

http_check.use_ssl.description: If true, use HTTPS instead of HTTP to run the check.
http_check.use_ssl.rationale: SSL usage is enforced indirectly via validate_ssl policy.

http_check.validate_ssl.description: Boolean specifying whether to include SSL certificate validation as a part of the Uptime check. Only applies to checks where 'monitored_resource' is set to 'uptime_url'. If 'use_ssl' is 'false', setting 'validate_ssl' to 'true' has no effect.
http_check.validate_ssl.rationale: Disabling SSL validation on HTTPS uptime checks allows the check to pass even when the certificate is invalid, expired, or issued by an untrusted authority, undermining transport security assurances.

http_check.accepted_response_status_code.description: If present, the check will only pass if the HTTP response status code is in this set of status codes. If empty, the HTTP status code will only pass if the HTTP status code is 200-299.
A class of status codes to accept. Possible values: ["STATUS_CLASS_1XX", "STATUS_CLASS_2XX", "STATUS_CLASS_3XX", "STATUS_CLASS_4XX", "STATUS_CLASS_5XX", "STATUS_CLASS_ANY"]
http_check.accepted_response_status_code.rationale: Functional configuration setting with no direct security impact.
Functional configuration setting with no direct security impact.

http_check.auth_info.description: The authentication information using username and password. Optional when creating an HTTP check; defaults to empty. Do not use with other authentication fields.

http_check.ping_config.description: Contains information needed to add pings to an HTTP check.

http_check.ping_config.pings_count.description: Number of ICMP pings. A maximum of 3 ICMP pings is currently supported.

http_check.service_agent_authentication.description: The authentication information using the Monitoring Service Agent. Optional when creating an HTTPS check; defaults to empty. Do not use with other authentication fields.

http_check.service_agent_authentication..description: The type of authentication to use. Possible values: ["SERVICE_AGENT_AUTHENTICATION_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED", "OIDC_TOKEN"]

monitored_resource.description:
The [monitored resource]
(https://cloud.google.com/monitoring/api/resources) associated with the
configuration. The following monitored resource types are supported for
uptime checks:
* 'aws_ec2_instance'
* 'aws_elb_load_balancer'
* 'gae_app'
* 'gce_instance'
* 'k8s_service'
* 'servicedirectory_service'
* 'uptime_url'

monitored_resource.labels.description: Values for all of the labels listed in the associated monitored resource descriptor. For example, Compute Engine VM instances use the labels 'project_id', 'instance_id', and 'zone'.
monitored_resource.labels.rationale: Functional identifiers with no security impact.

monitored_resource.type.description: The monitored resource type. This field must match the type field of a ['MonitoredResourceDescriptor'](https://cloud.google.com/monitoring/api/ref_v3/rest/v3/projects.monitoredResourceDescriptors#MonitoredResourceDescriptor) object. For example, the type of a Compute Engine VM instance is 'gce_instance'. For a list of types, see [Monitoring resource types](https://cloud.google.com/monitoring/api/resources) and [Logging resource types](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/api/v2/resource-list).
monitored_resource.type.rationale: Resource type selector with no direct security impact.

resource_group.description: The group resource associated with the configuration.

resource_group.group_id.description: The group of resources being monitored. Should be the 'name' of a group
resource_group.group_id.rationale: Functional configuration setting with no direct security impact.

resource_group.resource_type.description: The resource type of the group members. Possible values: ["RESOURCE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED", "INSTANCE", "AWS_ELB_LOAD_BALANCER"]
resource_group.resource_type.rationale: Functional configuration setting with no direct security impact.

synthetic_monitor.description: A Synthetic Monitor deployed to a Cloud Functions V2 instance.

synthetic_monitor.cloud_function_v2.description: Target a Synthetic Monitor GCFv2 Instance

synthetic_monitor.cloud_function_v2.name.description: The fully qualified name of the cloud function resource.
synthetic_monitor.cloud_function_v2.name.rationale: Identifier or display metadata with no security impact.

tcp_check.description: Contains information needed to make a TCP check.

tcp_check.port.description: The port to the page to run the check against. Will be combined with host (specified within the 'monitored_resource') to construct the full URL.
tcp_check.port.rationale: Operational setting with no direct security impact.

tcp_check.ping_config.description: Contains information needed to add pings to a TCP check.

tcp_check.ping_config.pings_count.description: Number of ICMP pings. A maximum of 3 ICMP pings is currently supported.
